options.text: Hello there.
Hey.
Hello, soldier.
Just wanted to say hi.
Thought I'd stop and say hello.
Hello again.
You there. Got a moment?
Busy? I can come back later.
Greetings from a weary traveler.
I come in peace.
Anyone up for a bit of conversation?
Hello, stranger.
Hail!
Good to see another living soul out here.
How goes it?
Well met.
Nice weather today, isn't it?
Miserable weather we're having.
Think it'll rain?
Cold enough for you?
This heat is something else.
That wind's really picking up.
Looks like a storm's brewing.
What's the sky telling you today?
Strange season this year, no?
Clear night. Look at those stars.
How's the war going?
Are you lot winning?
Any news from the front?
Seems quiet lately. Is it?
Think this war will ever end?
This war's costing everyone plenty.
Who has the upper hand these days?
Is it all worth it, do you think?
Rough month out there?
Still holding your ground out here?
What's your name?
What should I call you?
Who am I talking to?
I never caught your name.
Do you have a name, or just a rank?
Remind me of your name?
How's your day going?
How are you holding up?
Long shift?
You look tired.
Everything alright with you?
How are spirits around here?
Have you eaten today?
Getting any sleep out here?
Want to hear a joke?
What do you call a meal that fights back? Rations.
I asked a map for directions once. It folded under pressure.
Know any good jokes?
You look like you could use a laugh.
My boots have seen more of this war than most generals.
Is the soup here as dangerous as they say?
Good morning.
You're up early.
Fine sunrise today.
Morning. Quiet night, I hope?
Morning. Anything hot to drink around here?
Early start for both of us, I see.
Morning. I've been walking since first light.
Good evening.
You're on watch late.
Dark out tonight.
Couldn't sleep. Saw your light.
Long night ahead?
Good moon for walking tonight.
Night air has teeth this time of year.
I don't think we've met.
You're the first of your people I've spoken with.
Let me introduce myself — I'm new around here.
I've seen your banners around, never stopped to talk.
I've heard about your people. Wanted to meet one.
New face, I know. I'll keep it brief.
Just arrived in this region.
I'm not here to fight.
I know what you think of me.
What's done is done. I only want to talk.
Your people have been watching me. I noticed.
See? Empty hands.
For what it's worth, I'm not proud of what happened.
Can we still talk, after everything?
Is there a price on my head yet?
I came alone. That should count for something.
Hear me out before you decide anything.
I'll stay where you can see me.
There's blood between us. I know it.
Maybe someday I can make it right.
Surprised I'd show my face?
Fine camp you've got here.
Thanks for letting me through the gate.
Tight watch you keep around here.
Busy place. I'll stay out of the way.
These walls look like they've seen some action.
So this is home for you?
Just stopping in to pay my respects.
Good to be inside the walls for once.
You're a long way from your walls.
Out here all alone?
How's the road ahead?
Didn't expect to meet anyone out here.
Out on patrol, are you?
Mind if I walk with you a stretch?
Rough country, this.
Any trouble on the paths lately?
Officer. My respects.
Good day to you, commander.
Could I have a moment of your time, officer?
You're the one in charge here, I take it?
I won't waste your time, officer.
An honor to speak with you.
I don't want any trouble.
Just passing through, that's all.
Mind if I stop here a moment?
Easy. I'm only here to talk.
I'll keep my distance if that helps.
I mean your people no disrespect.
I think we got off on the wrong foot.
Any chance we could start over?
Tell me your rules and I'll follow them.
I'll be quick, then I'm gone.
Am I safe walking this road?
I'm not your enemy. Not today, anyway.
You have my word I'll behave.
Didn't mean to startle you.
So... are we good, you and I?
If I've wronged your people, tell me how to fix it.
Keep an eye on me if you want. I understand.
Am I still welcome here?
Don't raise an alarm. It's only me.
Look what the war dragged in.
Still alive, I see. Good habit.
You get uglier every time I visit.
Miss me?
There's my favorite soldier.
They haven't promoted you yet? Criminal.
Stayed out of trouble since I left?
How's my favorite band of troublemakers?
Hard at work, or hardly working?
You still owe me from that bet.
Got any gossip for me?
This place is starting to feel like home.
Try not to get killed while I'm gone, yeah?
Next round's on me, whenever you get leave.
Can't seem to stay away from you lot.
New helmet? Very dashing.
So who's winning — you or the boredom?
They tell stories about you at the other posts, you know.
Told you I'd come back in one piece.
I could smell the camp cooking a mile off. Came anyway.
How's the mud treating you?
Any chatter on the net worth hearing?
Is the kettle on?
Dug any good holes lately?
How do you bear all this sand?
Filed all your reports today?
Take care of yourself out here.
I'll leave you to your watch.
I'll get out of your way now.
See you around.
Right. This got awkward. Goodbye.
Safe watch. I'm off.
Your people run a tight operation.
Takes guts to do what you do.
That's fine gear you're carrying.
I respect what your people fight for.
You lot are tougher than you get credit for.
Best-run outfit I've seen anywhere.
You lot smell like a swamp died.
Heard your side's been taking a beating. Looks true.
Do they teach you that nervous look, or is it natural?

negative: Save the hello. Words are cheap and wire is expensive.
The line sees you. That is not a welcome.
You greet us like we forgot. We don't forget. We count.
neutral: Yeah. You're on the drainage board. Move left.
Hello, hello. The mud says hello too.
A greeting. Fine. What comes after it?
positive: There's that face. The trench is uglier without it.
Hey. Come over where the arrows don't land. Mostly don't.
The line greets you back, friend. That's rare as dry socks.

negative: Contact noted. Keep your distance and your hands empty.
Greeting received. Trust not included.
You're on the watch list, civilian. Hellos don't amend files.
neutral: Acknowledged. State your business or move along.
Receiving you. Keep the approach clear while we talk.
Contact logged, civilian. Proceed.
positive: Good copy. Always room on the net for a friendly.
Receiving you loud and clear, friend. Go ahead.
Cleared through. You picked a quiet hour — enjoy it.

negative: The jackal also says hello before it circles.
A greeting from you weighs less than the wind that carries it.
Words are water. Yours arrive salted.
neutral: Peace, walker. Small peace, but ours.
You greet the shade; the shade considers you.
The road brought you; let us see what else it brought.
positive: And peace upon you, friend of the quiet places.
The kettle heard your voice and is already warm.
Welcome twice — once for you, once for the news you carry.

negative: The weather is mud. You are also a problem. One of these we can fix.
Rain falls on friend and debtor alike. Only one of them should relax.
neutral: It rains, we dig, the trench drinks. Same forecast since forever.
Cold today. Cold tomorrow. The line doesn't check the sky, it checks the wire.
Sky's grey. Sky is always grey. It matches the uniforms.
positive: Ha — you learn. Talk weather first, bad news second. The trench way.
Good drying wind today. First dry socks in a week. A feast day.
Sun's out. The line distrusts it. Sun means someone sees you.

negative: Weather chat won't clear your file. Anything operational?
Visibility's fine. Good enough to keep eyes on you.
neutral: Ceiling's low, wind's manageable. That's the full report, civilian.
Forecast calls for rain over the sector by nightfall. Plan accordingly.
Weather's within parameters. Everything else, classified.
positive: Clear skies, friend. Best observation weather all week.
Front's moving in from the west. You'll want a roof by dusk — take the near road.
Nice enough that command scheduled drills. There's always a cost.

negative: You speak of the sky to avoid speaking of yourself. The sky notices.
Weather is the desert's mood. Today it shares mine. Be brief.
neutral: The wind turned east in the night. East winds carry news and grit.
Hot sun, cold stars. The desert keeps honest books.
Rain here is a rumor. We treat rumors with respect.
positive: For you, friend, I will say it: storm coming. Two days. Dig your camp deep.
The cool hours are kind today. Sit in them with us a while.
The sky is soft this evening. Even the scorpions are at peace.

negative: The war goes. You would know — you fed it.
Ask the ones we buried. Oh. You can't.
neutral: The war eats. We feed it. Some weeks it chews slow.
Front's quiet. Quiet is a debt the loud days collect on.
We hold. They push. The mud referees.
positive: Between us? We're winning slowly, which is the only speed we know.
War's the same. But the soup improved, so morale is up two percent.
The line held all month, friend. For us that's a parade.

negative: Operational status is not shared with flagged individuals.
The war proceeds. Your part in it is under review.
neutral: Situation is stable. Details are need-to-know, and you don't.
Contested sectors remain contested. That's all that's releasable.
The board shows amber. Amber is survivable.
positive: Off the record? We hold the ridge, they hold the marsh, nobody holds the middle.
Progress is real but slow, friend. Doctrine says patience. Doctrine wins.
Two sectors quieter than last season. Small wins log the same as big ones.

negative: The war is a fire. You ask how it burns while smelling of smoke.
It goes as the desert wills. The desert has opinions about you.
neutral: Wars are rivers. Loud at the rapids, patient underground. We are underground.
Ask the vulture, who sees the whole board. We only see our shade.
The strong tire. The desert does not. That is the whole war.
positive: Well, friend. The heavy ones chase our footprints; the footprints lead nowhere kind.
The war leans our way like an evening shadow — slowly, then all at once.
We lost nothing this month. For sand, that is victory.

negative: My name is none-of-yours. It's a common name here.
The dead had names. Ask about them instead.
neutral: Names wear out fast here. Call me what you like, I answer to shouting.
I'm the third one on the left, second trench. That's name enough.
positive: Ha! Nobody asks that. I'm Lev's boy — everyone here is somebody's boy.
They call me Shovel. Long story. Short shovel.

negative: You don't need my designation. You need distance.
Identity is operational information. Denied.
neutral: Callsigns only past the wire. Mine's whatever the roster says today.
You can address me as 'watchstander'. Everyone does.
positive: Off duty they call me Deuce. On duty I'm a post number. Take your pick.
Ask me again over rations sometime, friend. On post, I'm just the helmet.

negative: You collect names like a trapper collects tracks. Mine stays in the sand.
The desert gives names. It has not given you mine.
neutral: A name is a rope. I hand it only to those who won't pull.
Call me cousin. Out here everyone is a cousin or a corpse.
positive: For you? I am called Whisper-of-the-Well. My mother called me something shorter.
Names are gifts, friend. Mine is Sef. Spend it gently.

negative: My day was fine until the arithmetic walked up and said hello.
Alive. Annoyed. In that order.
neutral: Knee-deep in water, holding a wall. A classic.
Same day as yesterday. We reuse them to save supply.
My boots are dry. Ask nothing more, you'll spoil it.
positive: Better now — company that isn't trying to kill us is a luxury.
Good day. Nobody died and the soup had actual potato. Historic.

negative: My shift is fine. My watch list is one name longer. Guess whose.
Status: on duty. Yours: on notice.
neutral: Eight hours on, four off, all quiet. Textbook.
Routine patrol, routine watch. Routine is the goal.
Day's nominal. Keep it boring for me, will you?
positive: Honestly? Quiet watch, good rotation, and now a friendly face. Solid day.
Green across the board, friend. Days like this make you superstitious.

negative: My day is sand and patience. Your visit spends the patience.
It was quiet. The quiet had better manners than this.
neutral: The sun rose, the sun will fall. Between them I keep watch. It's enough.
A day like a date palm — long, thin, some sweetness at the top.
positive: Sweetened, now. Guests make the tea taste of occasion.
The shade is cool and my cousins are alive. A rich day, friend.

negative: We have a joke too. It has a punchline made of consequences.
Funny. The last funny one is on latrine duty forever. Careful.
neutral: Heh. Not bad. The mud laughed a little.
Why does the recruit dig two trenches? One is a spare grave. ...We laugh here.
positive: HA! I'm stealing that for the night watch. They need it.
Good one. Almost as funny as our supply schedule.

negative: Humor from you reads as provocation. Noted.
Laughter is not on my duty roster today. Neither are you.
neutral: Registered as humor. Response withheld pending review.
That's a smile. Off the record it never happened.
positive: Copy that joke. Retransmitting on the squad net tonight.
Ha — filing that under morale, subsection unofficial.

negative: The hyena laughs too. Ask him how the story ends.
A jest from a salted tongue still tastes of salt.
neutral: Mm. The desert's jokes are longer. Some take years to land.
A smile is a small oasis. I will camp at this one briefly.
positive: Ha! I will trade you one of ours: what did the dune say to the fortress? 'I have time.'
You joke like a cousin now. Dangerous. Cousins get chores.

negative: Morning. Another day you're still on our ledger.
The sun's up. It sees you too.
neutral: Morning. The line survived the night. Standard miracle.
It's morning if you call this light. We call it grey shift.
positive: Morning, friend! Tea's brutal today. Builds character.
A good morning — frost kept the mud honest overnight.

negative: Morning report includes you. That's not a compliment.
Dawn's here and so are you. State your purpose, keep it short.
neutral: Morning. Watch change in twenty. Make it quick.
Good morning, civilian. Sector was quiet overnight. Help it stay that way.
positive: Morning, friend. Dawn patrol found nothing but dew. Best possible news.
Good morning. First light was clean — you can see three ridges today.

negative: Dawn shows every footprint from the night. Yours included.
The morning is honest. Be honest with it.
neutral: Morning is the desert's truce. Even the snakes honor it. Speak.
The sun is young and merciful yet. State your need before it grows up.
positive: A blessed dawn, friend. First light was the color of good dates.
Morning, friend. The night passed like a well-paid guest — quietly.

negative: Wandering in the dark near our wire. Bold or stupid. Pick one, fast.
Night visit. Debt collectors do that too.
neutral: Night watch. Speak soft. Sound carries and so do arrows.
It's late. The line sleeps in shifts. I'm the shift.
positive: Up late too, friend? Sit. The dark is roomier than the day.
Quiet night. Almost suspiciously nice. Don't spoil it, ha.

negative: Night movement by a flagged individual. Be very transparent right now.
It's dark and you're on my list. Do the math and stay in the light.
neutral: Night watch, civilian. Stay in the lit lane and state your business.
You're on my optics. Approach slow, talk normal.
positive: Evening, friend. Stars are out and the net is quiet. Rare combination.
Night's calm. Stick to the marked path anyway — trust the tape, not the dark.

negative: The night is ours, walker. You borrow it. Borrowers pay.
Only owls and debtors travel this late. You don't look like an owl.
neutral: The desert opens at night. Mind what walks out of it.
Night is when we do our listening. You have our ears — briefly.
positive: Welcome to the cool hours, friend. This is when the desert tells the truth.
Sit by the small fire. Night guests bring the best stories.

negative: We haven't met, but your reputation dug in before you did.
New face, old story. Prove the story wrong.
neutral: First time at the line? Rule one: don't stand where I do.
New face. The mud takes all kinds. What do you want?
positive: So you're the one the others mentioned. Good things, mostly. Rare.
First meeting and no one's bleeding. Best introduction this month.

negative: No file on you yet. Files start today. Behave accordingly.
Unknown contact. You get exactly one first impression. Spend it well.
neutral: First contact logged. Name and business, in that order.
New to the sector? Read the postings, follow the tape, you'll do fine.
positive: Word travels ahead of you, friend, and for once it's favorable.
Fresh face, clean record. Cleanest thing in this sector. Welcome.

negative: New to me, not to the sand. It has already sketched you.
Strangers are unread letters. Some are bills.
neutral: A first meeting is a blank page. Ink carefully.
The desert introduces everyone eventually. Today it chose us. Speak.
positive: The wind spoke of a stranger with good manners. Sit, be the rumor.
First meetings under good stars. The tea decides if there's a second.

vengeful: Eleven graves and you bring me small talk. Say one more word worth digging for.
We drew lots for who avenges the eleventh. I lost. Or won. Depends on you.
negative: You say hello with our blood still in the arithmetic. Careful.
Talk soft. Half this trench wants your boots as souvenirs.
The count says eleven. Your mouth says hello. The count is louder.
neutral: We remember what you did. We also remember worse. Speak.
You've killed ours. The line notes it and keeps digging. State your business.
positive: There's blood between us and yet here you stand. That takes something. Talk.
The old count holds, but so does the new one. Lately you count better.

vengeful: Weapons-free is one signature away and my pen is warm. Speak very carefully.
Your name is read at our memorials — as the cause. Remember that with every word.
negative: You have confirmed kills on this command. Every word you say is evidence.
Personnel lost to you are posted on that wall. Look at it while you talk.
Approach ends at ten paces. The casualties in your file say so.
neutral: Your record includes our people. It also includes restraint since. Continue.
We log losses and we log conduct. Both are current. Speak.
positive: Your file has red pages, friend. It also has commendations after them. Odd read.
We don't forget our dead. We do read the whole ledger. Yours balances. Barely.

vengeful: Our dead have told the sand your stride, your scent, your habit of looking left.
I have carried your name in my mouth for a season. It tastes of iron.
negative: You greet us with hands the sand has tasted. It remembers the flavor.
Our dead drink first at every well you approach. Walk thirsty.
Hello, says the knife to the wound.
neutral: Blood dries. Debts don't. But debts can be carried politely. Speak.
The desert buried what you took from us. It buries grudges slower.
positive: You took from us once. Since then you give. The scale sways, friend. Keep it swaying.
Even a storm may become rain. Sit. The tea is not poisoned. A joke. Sit.

negative: You nod at our gate with your history? Nod and keep moving.
Inside the wire is a privilege. Yours is under review.
neutral: Nod received. Wipe your boots, don't touch the crates.
You're inside the wire. Act like it. Slow hands, short visits.
positive: Come in out of the wind, friend. Mind the third duckboard, it bites.
The gate knows you now. Almost family. Almost.

negative: You're inside a controlled perimeter with a flagged file. Escort is watching.
Base courtesy extends exactly as far as the exit. Note where it is.
neutral: Courtesy acknowledged. Stay in the common lanes, off the platforms.
Visitor protocol applies. Marked paths, no sketching, no souvenirs.
positive: At ease, friend. Mess tent's open if the smell doesn't scare you.
Good to have you on the inside for once. Green lanes are all yours.

negative: You stand in our shade uninvited. Shade can be withdrawn.
Guest-right is a rope bridge. Yours is fraying. Step lightly.
neutral: You are within our tents' shadow. Old rules hold: no blades bared, no lies told.
Guest-right given, guest-right measured. Sit where the carpets are worn.
positive: Our fire is your fire, friend. The good cushions, even.
Enter as family enters — loudly, and headed for the food.

negative: Far from witnesses, the two of us. Lucky for you the quota's filled today.
Out here the mud keeps secrets. Remember that and be polite.
neutral: Patrol's a loop. You're a bump in it. A quick bump, yes?
Long way from the line. Everything out here is either lost or hunting.
positive: Good to see a friendly face where there's usually only crows.
Walk a stretch with me, friend. The route's dull and you're not.

negative: You're outside my sector and inside my suspicion. Keep the gap.
No witnesses out here means I log carefully. Very carefully. Proceed.
neutral: Patrol contact. You're off the common routes. Reason?
This track's swept but not held. Travel it fast, not at dusk.
positive: A friendly on the trail — that's a good omen by any doctrine.
If you're heading north, friend, the ford's washed out. Use the stones east of it.

negative: Far from your walls, near to mine. Feel the difference.
The open desert is our courtroom. Walk like a defendant.
neutral: Two travelers, one horizon. Pass in peace or don't pass.
The trail is neutral ground. The trail's opinion can change.
positive: Well met between wells, friend. Rare and sweet, like rain.
The path favored us both today. Share dates? They're good this season.

negative: You address an officer of the line. It has a long memory and short patience.
Formality from you. Noted. My clerk notes everything else.
neutral: Correct address. Refreshing. State your matter, I have a front to run.
An officer's minute is rationed like everything here. You have one.
positive: At ease with me, friend of the line. Formality is for people we distrust.
You honor the rank; the rank remembers. Sit, my stove works.

negative: Your courtesy is registered. So are your incidents. The incidents weigh more.
Protocol received. Protocol will not shield you from consequence. Proceed.
neutral: Proper form. Appreciated. You have my attention until my next report is due.
State your matter with precision and I'll answer in kind.
positive: Courtesy met with courtesy, friend. My tent flap is open to you.
You speak like someone I'd commission. What do you need?

negative: You bow to the falcon while robbing its nest. The falcon sees both.
Fine manners on a dusty ledger. Manners do not settle accounts.
neutral: You honor the old forms. The old forms honor you back — precisely that far.
Speak. Rank in the desert means I answer for more graves. I listen carefully.
positive: Such courtesy, friend. Sit at my right; the shade is deeper there.
You greet me as the elders taught. For that, my time is yours.

negative: No trouble, he says. Trouble says that too, at first.
Passing through. Good. Pass faster.
You want peace? Cheap to say. Expensive to keep. We'll see.
neutral: Easy. Nobody's reaching for anything. Say your piece.
Fine. You're careful. Careful lives longer here.
positive: Relax, friend. Around us your shoulders can come down from your ears.
You worry too much. Save it for the siege days.

negative: Your caution is appropriate. Maintain it and this stays civil.
De-escalation acknowledged. You're still being observed.
Hands visible, voice level. Good instincts. Keep them.
neutral: No alert's been called. Keep it that way and we're fine.
Understood. You're compliant, we're professional. Simple.
positive: Stand easy, friend. You're not the threat picture today.
No need for formalities. You've got a clean lane here.

negative: The nervous goat bleats before the wolf arrives. Which are you?
You tread as if the sand were glass. Sand remembers weight, not steps.
Fear is a fair beginning. Wisdom is a better ending.
neutral: Be calm. If we wished you harm, the harm would not announce itself.
You may lower your voice's shield. We are only talking.
positive: Peace, friend, peace. Among us your shadow may sit down.
No need to walk on eggshells. This tent has thick carpets.

negative: We're not friends. Friends is a rank you haven't earned.
Banter is for people whose names aren't on my list.
neutral: Cheeky. The line tolerates cheeky on Tuesdays.
Careful, humor is contagious. Then the sergeant catches it and everyone suffers.
positive: There it is. Say that at the fire tonight — Pyotr owes me a laugh.
You've been drinking with our lot too long. You sound like us now.
Ha! Keep that up and we'll issue you a shovel.

negative: We are not familiar. Keep this professional.
You're chatting like we're friends. Check the record: we're not.
neutral: Witty. Not procedure, but witty.
I'd laugh, but I'm on duty. Consider it laughed at eighteen hundred.
positive: Unauthorized humor detected. Carry on.
Keep that up, friend, and I'll log you as squad morale equipment.
You joke like second squad. That's a compliment. Mostly.

negative: Jokes between us? The rope must come before the swing, stranger.
You tease like a cousin. You are not a cousin.
neutral: Careful with humor. Around here it ripens into obligations.
Half a smile for that. The other half costs news.
positive: Ha! You have a desert tongue now — dry and sharp.
Tell that one to my uncle. He will adopt you on the spot.
See how you jab, friend? Next you will haggle. Then you are truly one of us.

negative: Go. Take your history with you.
Leaving is your best idea today.
neutral: Off you go. Mind the wire on the way out.
Right. Back to the digging, then.
positive: Walk well, friend. Keep your head below the interesting parts of the sky.
Go on. Bring news next time. Or sausage. News or sausage.

negative: Departure noted with approval.
Exit's that way. Use the whole of it.
neutral: Copy. Contact terminated. Travel safe.
Understood. Clear the approach on your way.
positive: Safe roads, friend. Net's open if you need us.
Copy that. See you next rotation.

negative: The exit forgives faster than we do. Find it.
Go with the wind. Better yet, go faster than it.
neutral: Travel in the cool hours. The road repays the patient.
May you find water where the map shows none.
positive: Go gently, friend. The shade holds your seat.
Until the wind crosses our tracks again. Walk well.

negative: Flattery. The dead were flattered too, probably.
Save the honey. We eat bread here.
neutral: The line doesn't run on compliments, but they weigh nothing. Accepted.
Sturdy? We're what's left. What's left gets called sturdy.
positive: Ha, keep talking. Morale's cheaper than arrows and you're supplying it.
Careful, praise makes the recruits march taller. Then they get seen.

negative: Compliments from flagged persons are reviewed for motive.
Noted. Flattery has no effect on assessment. Ever.
neutral: Feedback logged. Discipline's not pretty, it's just correct.
Acknowledged. The polish is procedure; the edge is practice.
positive: Kind words, friend. I'll pass them up the chain — they're rare cargo.
Appreciated. Say it louder next time, my lieutenant needs the mood.

negative: Honey from your jar. We will check it for wasps.
Pretty words. The desert has heard prettier from thirstier mouths.
neutral: Praise is a coin. We bite it first — no offense meant.
You admire the falcon. Good. Admire it from where the talons aren't.
positive: May your tongue stay this sweet, friend. My cousins will want to hear it.
You honor us. In return: the west track floods at dusk. Avoid it.

negative: Mouth like that, this close to the wire. Some people dig their own quota.
Say it again. Slower. I want to remember it at your expense.
neutral: Rude. The line has heard worse from the sky. Still — watch it.
That mouth will cost you more than it earns. Free advice.
positive: Ha! Only a friend insults us that badly and walks. You walk — once.
Bold words, friend. I'd duck if I were your hat.

negative: Verbal aggression logged. You are now a pattern, not an incident.
That kind of talk moves you up a list you don't want to be on.
neutral: Disrespect noted for the record. The record is long and patient.
Say that to the duty officer. I'll wait. I'll enjoy waiting.
positive: I'll pretend the wind took that one, friend. Wind's taking exactly one today.
Cute. Your file now says 'comedian'. It's not a promotion.

negative: Spit at the desert and it returns to you on the wind. Always.
Words like broken glass. You will walk back over them barefoot.
neutral: An insult is a seed. Consider what you want growing on your road.
The tongue is a blade with no handle. You hold it badly.
positive: Ha — a friend's insult. Still, feed it to the fire before it grows.
Between friends, one such arrow is a joke. The second is an arrow.
